entities_included.other: No hospital or health system and no FFRDC is mentioned anywhere in the statements (text search for hospital/health/affiliat returned only the Maine Health and Higher Educational Facilities Authority bond issuer and post-retirement medical plan). Consolidated subsidiaries named in Note 1 (Basis of Presentation): Kostas Research Institute, New College of the Humanities (UK) and Marymount Manhattan College (MMC). Global campus system: Note 1 says 14 campuses across the U.S., U.K. and Canada; all consolidated. MMC became a Northeastern-controlled entity on June 16, 2025 (accounted for as an acquisition, ASC 958-805), so FY25 opex includes only about two weeks of MMC operations; MMC's opex is not disclosed. Inherent contribution recognized (nonoperating) $202,690,000.

calibration_fy23.explanation: No reference values were supplied for Northeastern, so the calibration block is skipped. For later comparison: FY23 S&W is not separable (only combined 'Salary and benefits' $1,050,908,000); FY23 core opex under the SPEC definition is $1,786,204,000.

student_counts_in_official_docs: None. The FY25, FY24 and FY23 audited statements contain no enrollment or student-count figures (text search for 'enrollment' returned nothing; 'students' appears only in descriptive text).
caveats: Northeastern reports only a combined 'Salary and benefits' line (statement of activities and Note 14), so salaries_and_wages is null and sw_combined_with_benefits carries the figure in all three years. No split is disclosed anywhere. The only partial benefit disclosure is the retirement plan contribution cost (Note 9): $65,412,000 FY25, $56,900,000 FY24, $44,915,000 FY23 (FY23 figure appears in both the FY24 report and the FY23 report Note 9). Other benefits (health, payroll tax, tuition remission) are not disclosed, so an S&W-only figure cannot be derived from the statements.

Amortization: no amortization line exists in operating expenses. Note 14 says functional categories 'include allocations of ... depreciation and amortization expense' but the natural columns are only Salary and Benefits, Other Operating Expenses, Depreciation and Interest. Amortization (if any, e.g. right-of-use assets or debt premium) is therefore embedded in Other operating expenses or Interest and is not separable. amortization set to null / amortization_in_opex false.

Interest: the statement-of-activities Interest line (the figure used, per SPEC) is lower than the 'Interest expense on bonds and notes payable' disclosed in the debt note: FY25 $49,862,000 vs $60,042,000 (gap $10,180,000); FY24 $35,970,000 vs $40,936,000 (gap $4,966,000, same in FY24 report); FY23 $41,452,000 vs $53,367,000 (gap $11,915,000). The statements do not explain the gap (no capitalized-interest disclosure found; swap settlements are mentioned for FY23/FY24 cash paid). If the debt-note figure were the right interest number, FY25 core opex would be about $10.2M (0.5%) lower. Kept the operating-expense line as shown.

Operating lease cost is not a separate line, so it presumably sits inside 'Other operating expenses' and is not removed: total rental expense on operating leases (incl. short-term and variable) was $156,462,000 FY25 and $140,120,000 FY24 (FY25 report, Note 7 Leases, PDF p21-22).

Cross-check: natural-classification totals in Note 14 equal total operating expenses on the statement of activities in all three years (FY25 2,388,249; FY24 2,224,534; FY23 1,949,746, thousands). Salary and benefits + other operating + depreciation + interest sums verified.

FY24 figures taken from the FY25 report and from the FY24 report agree exactly (1,236,189 / 134,195 / 35,970 / 2,224,534). FY23 figures in the FY24 report and in the FY23 report agree exactly. No restatement found.

FY25 comparability: Marymount Manhattan College joined June 16, 2025 (about two weeks of MMC operations in FY25 opex). All campuses in the 14-campus global system (U.S., U.K., Canada) are inside the consolidated totals; no per-campus expense split is disclosed.
